lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 3 you met word meanings. Which word means the same as big: large or little? Large. Words that mean the same are synonyms.
When you meet a new word, look at the words around it: its context. They often give a clue to what it means.
A definition clue: The cavern, a huge cave under the hill, was dark. The words after the comma tell you what a cavern is.
An opposite clue: Unlike his timid sister, Leo was brave. Timid must mean the opposite of brave: shy and easily scared.
Synonyms are words that mean the same or nearly the same (big, large). Antonyms mean the opposite (big, small).
Try it in the world: open one of the game's Books and find a word you don't know. Use the words around it to guess what it means, then ask a grown-up to check. Next: similes, metaphors and idioms.

exercises.prompt: Which word is a synonym of "happy"?
exercises.hint: A synonym means the same.
exercises.explain: Glad and happy mean nearly the same.

exercises.prompt: Which word is an antonym of "hot"?
exercises.hint: An antonym means the opposite.
exercises.explain: Cold is the opposite of hot.

exercises.prompt: Which word is a synonym of "quick"?
exercises.hint: Which word could you swap for quick in "a quick run"?
exercises.explain: Fast and quick mean the same.

exercises.prompt: "Tiny" and "huge" are antonyms.
exercises.hint: Are they opposites?
exercises.explain: Yes: tiny and huge are opposites.

exercises.prompt: The pup was famished, so it ate three bowls of food. What does "famished" mean?
exercises.hint: Why would a pup eat three bowls?
exercises.explain: Eating three bowls is the clue: famished means very hungry.

exercises.prompt: The path was so narrow that only one person could walk on it at a time. What does "narrow" mean?
exercises.hint: Only one person fits.
exercises.explain: Only one person fits, so narrow means not wide.

exercises.prompt: Unlike the noisy market, the library was tranquil. What does "tranquil" mean?
exercises.hint: "Unlike" tells you it is the opposite of noisy.
exercises.explain: Tranquil is the opposite of noisy: calm and quiet.

exercises.prompt: Which word is an antonym of "ancient"?
exercises.hint: Ancient means very old.
exercises.explain: New is the opposite of ancient.

exercises.prompt: "Begin" and "start" are synonyms.
exercises.hint: Do they mean the same?
exercises.explain: Yes: begin and start mean the same.

exercises.prompt: The buddy was reluctant to jump into the cold lake; it stood at the edge for ages. What does "reluctant" mean?
exercises.hint: It waited at the edge for ages.
exercises.explain: Waiting at the edge shows it did not want to jump: reluctant means not wanting to.

exercises.prompt: The explorer found a hatchling, a baby bird that had just come out of its egg. What kind of clue explains "hatchling"?
exercises.hint: Read what comes after the comma.
exercises.explain: The words after the comma tell you exactly what a hatchling is.

exercises.prompt: The soup was bland, not spicy or salty at all. What does "bland" mean?
exercises.hint: The sentence says it is not spicy and not salty. What is left?
exercises.explain: Not spicy or salty at all: bland means without much taste.

exercises.prompt: Which pair are antonyms?
exercises.hint: Find the opposites.
exercises.explain: Generous (happy to share) is the opposite of selfish.

exercises.prompt: After the long climb, Nia was weary and sat down to rest. Which word is a synonym of "weary"?
exercises.hint: Why did she sit down to rest?
exercises.explain: A long climb and a rest: weary means tired.

exercises.prompt: In "The room was spotless, with not one speck of dust", spotless means very dirty.
exercises.hint: Could a room with not one speck of dust be dirty?
exercises.explain: No: not one speck of dust means spotless is very clean.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to its antonym.
exercises.hint: An antonym means the opposite. Say each word, then its opposite.
exercises.explain: ancient: new. generous: selfish. noisy: quiet. narrow: wide.

exercises.prompt: Sort the clues in these sentences.
items: A cavern, a huge cave, lay ahead.
Unlike noisy streets, the library was tranquil.
A foal, a baby horse, ran by.
He was timid, not brave at all.
exercises.hint: Does the sentence say what the word means, or what it is not like?
exercises.explain: The cavern and the foal are explained after a comma: definition clues. Unlike noisy streets and not brave at all tell you the opposite: opposite clues.

exercises.prompt: Sort the pairs: synonyms or antonyms?
exercises.hint: Do the two words mean the same, or the opposite?
exercises.explain: Synonyms mean the same: begin and start, weary and tired, glad and happy. Antonyms are opposites: ancient and new, timid and brave, bland and spicy.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to its meaning, using the clues you met.
exercises.hint: Remember the sentences: three bowls of food, a quiet library, a buddy at the lake's edge, a long climb.
exercises.explain: Famished: very hungry (three bowls). Tranquil: calm and quiet (unlike the market). Reluctant: not wanting to (it stood at the edge). Weary: tired (after the climb).

exercises.prompt: Put the steps for working out a new word in order.
items: Check with a grown-up or a dictionary.
Spot the word you don't know.
exercises.hint: What must you notice before you can look for clues?
exercises.explain: Spot the new word, read the words around it for a clue, make a guess, then check it with a grown-up or a dictionary.

exercises.prompt: Use each sentence's clue to match its new word (glacier, bold, murky) to a meaning.
items: The glacier, a river of ice
Unlike the shy pup, Rex was bold
Murky water: too dark to see
exercises.hint: Look for the words after a comma, the word 'unlike', and the words that describe the water.
exercises.explain: Glacier: a slow river of ice (a definition after the comma). Bold: brave (unlike shy, its opposite). Murky: cloudy and dark (too dark to see).

exercises.prompt: Sort the words: do they mean big or small?
exercises.hint: Put each word in 'a ___ elephant': does it make the elephant bigger or smaller?
exercises.explain: Huge, large and enormous mean big, so they are synonyms of each other. Tiny, little and teeny mean small. The two groups are antonyms: opposites.
